newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: SABIC shareholders approve 2.5 bln riyal dividend.
newsitem.headline: SABIC shareholders approve 2.5 bln riyal dividend.

text.p: Shareholders of Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) has approved a 2.5 billion riyal ($666.7 million) dividend for 1996, or 25 riyals per share.
A company statement said on Monday the approval was made at a shareholders' meeting in the Saudi capital Riyadh on Sunday.
The 2.5 billion riyal dividend is down from three billion riyals approved for 1995.

SABIC, 70 percent owned by the Saudi government, made a net profit of 4.412 billion riyals in 1996, down 30 percent from 6.281 billion riyals in 1995. It attributed the decline in profit to lower prices in the world petrochemical market.
Saudi Industry and Electricity Minister and SABIC'S chairman Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani said SABIC would continue to implement expansion programmes to raise its production capacity.

"These expansions are expected to give SABIC a clear advantage when world petrochemical prices move up again in the coming years, in terms of both profitability and its ability to meet the anticipated increase in demand," Yamani said.

SABIC, which accounts for around five percent of the world's petrochemical production, has embarked in an ambitious programme to raise its annual production capacity to 28 million tonnes by the year 2000 from the current 23 million tonnes.
It controls and operates 16 petrochemical complexes with Western and Japanese companies, producing mainly petrochemicals, plastics, fertilisers and steel.
